specification.problem: Evaluate a Boolean formula over an extended gate set (all 2- and 3-bit gates, e.g., NAND, 3-majority) on an input x in {0,1}^n using a quantum algorithm built from a correspondence between span programs and weighted bipartite graphs: the span program evaluates to 1 on x exactly when the associated graph G_P(x) has an eigenvalue-zero eigenvector supported on the output vertex, which is detected by spectral (phase) estimation.
specification.reconstruction_scope: Single-gate instance: a span program for the 3-bit majority gate MAJ3 on input x=(x_1,x_2,x_3), its associated bipartite graph with biadjacency matrix B_x (input-vector columns deleted when the literal is false), the eigenvalue-zero eigenvector criterion, and a phase-estimation routine on exp(-i A_{G(x)}) started at the output vertex that accepts iff an eigenvalue-zero component is detected. Outside scope: composition of span programs into full read-once formulas, the paper's choice of edge weights/normalizations, the 'balanced inputs' condition and optimality (query-complexity) proofs, the spectral-gap analysis that fixes the phase-estimation precision, and the AND-OR special case.

symbols.meaning: Boolean input string to the formula/gate
Span program with target vector and input vectors, each input vector labelled by a literal of x
Set of indices j whose labelling literal is true on x (available input vectors)
Boolean function computed by span program P
Biadjacency matrix of the bipartite graph G_P(x): rows indexed by the d coordinates, columns by the output vertex (target) and the available input-vector vertices
Basis state of the output (target) vertex of G_P(x)
Primitive cube root of unity used in the MAJ3 span program instance
Phase-estimation precision; must be below the smallest nonzero |eigenvalue| relevant when f_P(x)=0

equations.label: Span program evaluation
equations.description: A span program accepts x exactly when the target lies in the span of the input vectors whose literals are true on x.
equations.justification: Standard definition of the span-program model (Karchmer–Wigderson); the abstract names the model but does not define it.
assumptions: Monotone-free (general) span programs with literals x_j and \bar{x}_j allowed.

equations.label: Associated bipartite graph
equations.description: Weighted bipartite graph whose left vertices are the d coordinates and right vertices are the output vertex (target) and the available input-vector vertices; edge weights are vector entries.
equations.abstract_quote: a correspondence between a classical linear-algebraic model of computation, "span programs," and weighted bipartite graphs
equations.justification: The abstract asserts a correspondence between span programs and weighted bipartite graphs; the natural realization is to take the span-program vectors as columns of a biadjacency matrix. The precise handling of unavailable vectors (deleted here) and the paper's weight normalizations are not given in the abstract.
assumptions: Unavailable input vectors are modelled by deleting their columns; the paper may instead attach dangling input vertices, which is equivalent for the zero-eigenvector criterion but changes register size.

equations.label: Eigenvalue-zero eigenvector criterion
equations.description: A zero-eigenvalue eigenvector of the graph supported on the output vertex exists iff the span program accepts; the witness coefficients a_j give the eigenvector on the right-hand vertices.
equations.abstract_quote: A span program's evaluation corresponds to an eigenvalue-zero eigenvector of the associated graph.
equations.justification: Direct consequence of eq_1 and eq_2: B_x applied to the right-side vector (1,-a_{j_1},...,-a_{j_k}) equals |t\rangle-\sum a_j|v_j\rangle=0, so it is in the kernel of A_{G(x)} with nonzero output-vertex amplitude; conversely any kernel vector with nonzero output amplitude yields a spanning witness.

equations.label: Tiny instance: span program for 3-majority
equations.description: Any two distinct |v_j\rangle span \mathbb{C}^2 (hence contain |t\rangle), while no single |v_j\rangle is proportional to |t\rangle, so acceptance iff at least two inputs are 1.
equations.justification: A valid minimal span program for MAJ3 chosen for the scoped instance; the paper's specific vectors and weight normalizations (which affect optimality constants) are not available from the abstract.
assumptions: Vector choice and normalization are this reconstruction's choice, not verified against the paper.

equations.label: Spectral estimation decision rule
equations.description: Phase estimation on the graph's Hamiltonian evolution starting at the output vertex; accept when the estimated eigenvalue is zero to within precision \delta. \psi_0 is the normalized projection of |out\rangle onto the zero-eigenspace.
equations.justification: The abstract states the quantum computer 'evaluate[s] the span program by applying spectral estimation to the graph'; this is the standard phase-estimation realization. The required \delta (set by the spectral gap away from zero when f_P(x)=0) and the resulting query complexity are the paper's analysis and are not reconstructed here.
assumptions: Phase estimation with p\approx\lceil\log_2(1/\delta)\rceil ancilla qubits and controlled-U_x^{2^k} is used; the paper may instead use a discrete quantum walk (product of reflections), which has the same zero-eigenvector criterion.

registers.name: vertex
registers.role: Encodes a vertex of G_P(x): coordinates 0..d-1 on the left side, output vertex d, input-vector vertex d+j for j=1..m (unavailable vertices unused when x_j=0).

registers.name: phase
registers.role: Phase-estimation precision register; p qubits in integer encoding, most-significant bit first, estimate \tilde{\lambda}=2\pi\,k/2^p (mod 2\pi) for measured k.

specification.initial_state: |0\rangle^{\otimes p}\otimes|\mathrm{out}\rangle, i.e., phase register all zeros and the vertex register in the output-vertex basis state (index d=2 for the MAJ3 instance).

steps.description: Classically (or via the input oracle) determine the available vector set I(x) and form the graph G_P(x) with Hamiltonian A_{G(x)} for the MAJ3 span program.
Prepare the initial state with the vertex register at the output vertex |out\rangle.
Apply Hadamards to the phase register, then controlled-U_x^{2^k} (U_x=e^{-iA_{G(x)}}) from phase qubit k onto the vertex register, then the inverse quantum Fourier transform on the phase register.
Measure the phase register and decide f_P(x) from whether the estimated eigenvalue is zero within precision \delta.

specification.measurement: Measure the p-qubit phase register in the computational basis, obtaining integer k; the estimated eigenvalue is \tilde{\lambda}=2\pi k/2^p reduced to (-\pi,\pi].
specification.classical_postprocessing: Output f_P(x)=1 if |\tilde{\lambda}|<\delta, else output 0. Repeat O(1) times and take majority to boost success probability; \delta must be smaller than the smallest nonzero |eigenvalue| of A_{G(x)} components reachable from |out\rangle when f_P(x)=0 (gap value not reconstructed).
assumptions: No experiment_scope was supplied; the smallest useful construction chosen is a single MAJ3 gate span program with the explicit vectors of eq_4.
Unavailable input vectors are deleted from the graph rather than attached to dangling input vertices.
Spectral estimation is realized as standard phase estimation on e^{-iA_{G(x)}}; the paper may use a different unitary (e.g., product of reflections / quantum walk).
Edge weights equal the span-program vector entries without the paper's optimality-driven rescaling.
missing_information: The paper's exact span programs and weightings for each 2- and 3-bit gate, including the MAJ3 vectors and normalizations.
